rationale: iter-17 Charbonnier loss (eps=1e-3) + SWA on iter-7 K=2 U-Net + BF. Headroom 0.5686 vs iter-16 (SWA + MSE) 0.5762 (-0.8pp) and vs iter-7 (MSE no avg) 0.5745 (-0.6pp). Charbonnier underperforms because at eps=1e-3 and typical target residuals ~0.005, the loss is in the L1 regime almost everywhere (linear in |diff|), giving HALF the gradient magnitude of MSE near zero. The model never reaches the loss plateau the MSE version does (Charbonnier loss=0.01179 at ep5, still trending; MSE plateaus at 0.00037 by ep5). 6 epochs is insufficient for L1-like loss on this scale. Could test with eps=1e-2 (push back to L2 regime) but Charbonnier appears wrong tool here.
advice_for_others: For dual-domain N2I CT recon at small target amplitudes (~0.005), Charbonnier at eps=1e-3 silently becomes L1 and halves the near-zero gradient — sticking with MSE or using eps comparable to target scale is safer.
